usage: PR quality gates for RepoVisUI, evaluated first-match-wins from the top with the same ordering as .codescene/code-health-rules.json. Gates answer a different question from rules: the rules file decides what is measured, this file decides what blocks a pull request, so the two are ordered the same way and read together. The one path whose content cannot be changed here - the regenerated `next-env.d.ts` type stub - turns every gate off. Every first-party source family turns all six gates on, and `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false in every gate map, so a critical-rule finding is reported against the code in front of the pull request and nothing else, which is the only coherent setting for a repository that is 100 percent coding-agent authored (package.json:2 `ai-studio-applet`, the AI Studio applet manifest in metadata.json, and the agent turn log in docs/journal.md). The `**/*` catch-all names the `pay_down_tech_debt` profile instead of a map, so a pull request touching build configuration, or a directory that has no measured rule set yet, may pay debt down instead of being blocked by a file no refactoring goal targets. No gate in this file depends on anything except the code in front of it.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The Next.js type-reference stub, regenerated by `next dev` / `next build` and marked at next-env.d.ts:5 `// NOTE: This file should not be edited`. No gate applies: a pull request cannot be asked to improve a file its own build rewrites, and `cs review` returns {"score":null,"review":[]} for it in any case.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All seven keys false. Any health signal on this path is the installed Next version's, not this repository's, so a gate that fired here would only teach an agent to hand-edit generated output.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The Vitest suite (tests/Dashboard.test.tsx, drift.test.ts, gravity.test.ts, utils.test.ts and the tests/setup.ts harness), run by `npm run test` -> `vitest run` per package.json:13. Every gate is on: a wrong green result hides every other defect in the repository, and the suite is the only executable proof that lib/analysis/ still returns what app/api/analyze/ promises.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All six enabled gates on; `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false. `new_code_health` and `hotspot_decline` matter most here: the suite is small enough that a copied module or a nested helper chain is a deliberate act, and the gate is what makes it a reviewed one.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The pure analysis primitives lib/analysis/drift.ts and lib/analysis/gravity.ts, consumed by app/api/analyze/route.ts:35 and :65 and tested directly by tests/drift.test.ts and tests/gravity.test.ts. Every gate is on: a wrong rule matrix silently mislabels every repository the dashboard is pointed at, and there is no runtime error to catch it.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All six enabled gates on; `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false. `critical_health_rules` is what enforces the 150-code-line cap this directory carries in code-health-rules.json.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The shared library layer: lib/audio.ts (the SoundSynth Web Audio class), lib/exhibits.ts (the MOCK_EXHIBITS data the dashboard renders), lib/logger.ts and lib/utils.ts. Every gate is on so a change here cannot land as a silent rewrite of the data every exhibit reads.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All six enabled gates on; `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false. lib/audio.ts is at 8.54 with real findings (`stopAmbient` cc 10, two complex conditionals), so `new_code_health` is the gate that stops a new synth voice from making the existing ones worse.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The React hook layer, today hooks/use-mobile.ts (`useIsMobile()` over matchMedia). Every gate is on: a hook defect is a render-time defect in every consumer, and the 50-code-line function cap in code-health-rules.json is only meaningful if a pull request that crosses it is stopped.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All six enabled gates on; `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false. `advisory_health_rules` is deliberately not relaxed for hooks: a nested conditional in a hook body is a concurrent-rendering bug, not style advice.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The server boundary, today app/api/analyze/route.ts - the single `GET` handler that walks lib/ and serialises the analysis results. Every gate is on: this is the only route whose response other code consumes, and the 60-code-line function cap is enforced by the gates or not at all.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All six enabled gates on; `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false. `supervise_goals` stays on so that a route rewrite cannot quietly drop a refactoring goal that the handler is holding open.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The App Router pages and server actions (app/page.tsx, app/hero/, app/startup/, app/svg-showcase/, app/layout.tsx and app/hero/actions.ts). Every gate is on, which is the strictest statement in this file: app/page.tsx is 2177 cs-measured code lines and scores 4.30, so any pull request that touches it has to leave it no worse than it found it.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All six enabled gates on; `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false. The consequence is stated plainly rather than engineered away: until app/page.tsx is split, a pull request that adds a twelfth exhibit to it will be blocked by `critical_health_rules`, and the way through is to land the exhibit in its own module, not to toggle a gate.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: Catch-all, deliberately last: the root build configuration (next.config.ts, vitest.config.ts, eslint.config.mjs, postcss.config.mjs) and any directory a future change introduces, which has no measured rule set behind it yet.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: The `pay_down_tech_debt` profile rather than a map, so a pull request on an unmapped path may pay debt down instead of being blocked. Promotion is explicit: the path gets its own gate set when code-health-rules.json gets one, and the two are promoted in the same change.
